statements.label: supported
statements.text: Carriers of rs17437411 show lower blood counts overall and are less likely to develop blood cancers.
statements.evidence: we identified a genetic variant, rs17437411, associated with globally reduced blood counts, protection from blood cancers, and variation in anthropometric phenotypes
statements.note: The abstract reports the variant as associated with globally reduced blood counts and protection from blood cancers.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: HOTSCRAMBL supports correct HOXA transcript expression and splicing in hematopoietic stem cells, with HOXA9 the clearest case, and this requires SRSF2.
statements.evidence: HOTSCRAMBL enables appropriate expression and splicing of HOXA genes in HSCs, most notably HOXA9, in an SRSF2-dependent manner
statements.note: The abstract states the SRSF2-dependent role of HOTSCRAMBL in HOXA expression and splicing, singling out HOXA9.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Restoring HOTSCRAMBL activity in variant-carrying hematopoietic stem cells returns their self-renewal capacity to wild-type levels.
statements.evidence: The HOTSCRAMBL variant disrupts lncRNA function and reduces human hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) self-renewal.
statements.note: The abstract reports what losing HOTSCRAMBL function does but says nothing about restoring it or whether self-renewal would recover.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Removing HOTSCRAMBL or carrying its variant form weakens acute myeloid leukemias that depend on HOXA.
statements.evidence: we also demonstrate that HOTSCRAMBL variation or deletion compromises HOXA-dependent acute myeloid leukemias
statements.note: The abstract directly reports that HOTSCRAMBL variation or deletion compromises HOXA-dependent AMLs.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Roughly two out of five of the 1416 surveyed giant virus genomes carried antibiotic resistance genes, a rate about 37-fold above that of phage genomes.
statements.evidence: We reveal that 39.5% of them carry ARGs, which is approximately 37 times higher than that for phage genomes.
statements.note: The abstract gives 39.5% of the 1416 NCLDV genomes and the roughly 37-fold comparison with phages.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Giant viruses transfer their antibiotic resistance genes to bacteria during co-infection of the same host cell.
statements.evidence: Phylogenies of the three most abundant NCLDV-encoded ARGs hint that NCLDVs acquire ARGs from not only eukaryotes but also prokaryotes and phages.
statements.note: The abstract addresses where the viruses got their ARGs from, not whether they hand them onward to bacteria or by what route.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Two trimethoprim resistance genes taken from giant virus genomes made Escherichia coli resistant to trimethoprim when tested.
statements.evidence: Two NCLDV-encoded trimethoprim resistance genes are demonstrated to confer trimethoprim resistance in Escherichia coli.
statements.note: The abstract reports this functional demonstration in E. coli.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Giant virus genomes that carry antibiotic resistance genes also tend to carry mobile genetic elements and virulence factors.
statements.evidence: The presence of ARGs in NCLDV genomes is significantly correlated with mobile genetic elements and virulence factors.
statements.note: The abstract reports a significant correlation between ARG presence and both mobile genetic elements and virulence factors.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: TBL1XR1 mutation pushes the antibody response toward aberrant immature memory B cells while blocking differentiation into plasma cells.
statements.evidence: TBL1XR1 mutations skew the humoral immune response toward generating abnormal immature memory B cells (MB), while impairing plasma cell differentiation
statements.note: The abstract reports exactly this dual effect of TBL1XR1 mutation on the humoral response.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mutant TBL1XR1 redirects SMRT/HDAC3 repressor complexes onto BACH2 rather than BCL6, reprogramming cells toward a pre-memory state.
statements.evidence: TBL1XR1 mutants co-opt SMRT/HDAC3 repressor complexes toward binding the MB cell transcription factor (TF) BACH2 at the expense of the germinal center (GC) TF BCL6, leading to pre-memory transcriptional reprogramming and cell-fate bias
statements.note: The abstract describes this redirection of SMRT/HDAC3 from BCL6 to BACH2 and the resulting reprogramming.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: HDAC inhibitor treatment reverses the cell-fate bias caused by TBL1XR1 mutation in memory B cells.
statements.evidence: At the molecular level, TBL1XR1 mutants co-opt SMRT/HDAC3 repressor complexes toward binding the MB cell transcription factor (TF) BACH2 at the expense of the germinal center (GC) TF BCL6, leading to pre-memory transcriptional reprogramming and cell-fate bias.
statements.note: The abstract names HDAC3 as part of the mechanism but reports no drug treatment or attempt to reverse the phenotype.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: After antigen re-exposure, TBL1XR1 mutant memory B cells preferentially return to germinal centers instead of becoming plasma cells.
statements.evidence: Upon antigen recall, TBL1XR1 mutant MB cells fail to differentiate into plasma cells and instead preferentially reenter new GC reactions
statements.note: The abstract reports this failure to differentiate and preferential germinal centre reentry on antigen recall.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Weight loss in obese individuals shifts the transcriptional cargo of circulating extracellular vesicles back toward the lean profile.
statements.evidence: We characterized circulating extracellular vesicles (EVs) in obese and lean humans, identifying transcriptional cargo differentially expressed in obesity (277 unique genes; false discovery rate < 10%).
statements.note: The abstract compares obese and lean people at one point but reports no intervention or follow-up after weight change.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study flagged 277 distinct genes whose expression in circulating extracellular vesicles differed with obesity at a false discovery rate under 10%.
statements.evidence: identifying transcriptional cargo differentially expressed in obesity (277 unique genes; false discovery rate < 10%)
statements.note: The abstract gives the count of 277 unique genes and the FDR threshold below 10%.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Transcripts from circulating extracellular vesicles agreed closely with those from visceral adipose tissue extracellular vesicles of the same obese donors.
statements.evidence: we compared this obesity EV transcriptome with expression from human visceral-adipose-tissue-derived EVs from freshly collected and cultured biopsies from the same obese individuals, observing high concordance
statements.note: The abstract reports high concordance between the circulating EV transcriptome and visceral adipose EVs from the same individuals.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A phenome-wide association study of the regulatory SNPs behind the extracellular-vesicle transcripts turned up a marked excess of inflammatory phenotypes, type 2 diabetes among them.
statements.evidence: Using a phenome-wide association study of the regulatory SNPs for the EV-derived transcripts, we identified a substantial enrichment for inflammatory phenotypes, including type 2 diabetes.
statements.note: The abstract reports the substantial enrichment for inflammatory phenotypes including type 2 diabetes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The atlas was built by combining bulk RNA-seq from 7,015 samples, single-cell data covering 127,598 cells, and 2,869 whole genomes, spanning 28 chicken tissues.
statements.evidence: we integrated bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data from 7,015 samples, single-cell RNA-seq data from 127,598 cells and 2,869 whole-genome sequences to present a pilot atlas of regulatory variants across 28 chicken tissues
statements.note: The abstract lists these exact data volumes and the number of tissues covered.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Regulatory effects detected in the atlas reach beyond protein-coding gene expression to alternative splicing and 3'-UTR alternative polyadenylation.
statements.evidence: This atlas reveals millions of regulatory effects on primary expression (protein-coding genes, long non-coding RNA and exons) and post-transcriptional modifications (alternative splicing and 3'-untranslated region alternative polyadenylation).
statements.note: The abstract reports regulatory effects on both primary expression and these post-transcriptional processes.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Selecting on the regulatory variants in the atlas raises growth rate in commercial broiler flocks.
statements.evidence: We highlighted distinct molecular mechanisms underlying these regulatory variants, their context-dependent behavior and their utility in interpreting genome-wide associations for 39 chicken complex traits.
statements.note: The abstract reports using the variants to interpret trait associations, not any breeding trial or measured gain in commercial birds.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Comparing gene regulation in chickens against mammals showed the resource can support mapping complex traits across species.
statements.evidence: our comparative analyses of gene regulation between chickens and mammals demonstrate how this resource can facilitate cross-species gene mapping of complex traits
statements.note: The abstract reports this chicken-mammal comparison and its use for cross-species gene mapping.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: IS607-family elements studied here carry group I introns, unlike the IS605-family TnpB systems described before.
statements.evidence: we uncovered molecular mechanisms of the transposition life cycle of IS607-family elements that, notably, also encode group I introns
statements.note: The abstract states that the IS607-family elements investigated also encode group I introns.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The Clostridium botulinum IStron can be reprogrammed as a genome-editing tool in human cells.
statements.evidence: We identified specific features for a candidate "IStron" from Clostridium botulinum that allow the element to carefully control the relative levels of spliced products versus functional guide RNAs.
statements.note: The abstract describes the element's own regulation and says nothing about adapting it for editing in any heterologous or human system.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A candidate IStron from Clostridium botulinum has features that let it tune how much spliced product it makes versus functional guide RNA.
statements.evidence: We identified specific features for a candidate "IStron" from Clostridium botulinum that allow the element to carefully control the relative levels of spliced products versus functional guide RNAs.
statements.note: The abstract reports these features controlling the ratio of spliced products to functional guide RNAs.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: IStron transcripts appear to have evolved a balance between two incompatible activities: selfish spread of the transposon and keeping host fitness costs down.
statements.evidence: Our results suggest that IStron transcripts evolved an ability to balance competing and mutually exclusive activities that promote selfish transposon spread while limiting adverse fitness costs on the host.
statements.note: The abstract states this balancing of mutually exclusive activities as its result.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The reported workflow draws on patient-specific genome-scale metabolic models together with mutation data to produce metabolite-gene-pathway sets.
statements.evidence: The computational workflow uses both cancer patient-specific genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) and mutation data to generate metabolite-gene-pathway sets.
statements.note: The abstract states that the workflow combines patient-specific GEMs and mutation data for this purpose.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Blocking one of the predicted oncometabolite-associated metabolic pathways slowed tumour growth in treated cells.
statements.evidence: Therapeutic potential of the resulting metabolite-gene-pathway sets is also discussed.
statements.note: The abstract says therapeutic potential is discussed but reports no experiment inhibiting a pathway or measuring an effect on tumour growth.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: First validation used acute myeloid leukemia and renal cell carcinoma samples gathered for this study, checking predicted metabolite-gene pairs against mutation, RNA-seq and metabolome data.
statements.evidence: The computational workflow is first validated by comparing the resulting metabolite-gene pairs with multi-omics data (i.e., mutation data, RNA-seq data, and metabolome data) from acute myeloid leukemia and renal cell carcinoma samples collected in this study.
statements.note: The abstract describes this first validation step, its data types and the two cancers used.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A second validation extended the predictions to 18 cancer types using publicly available RNA-seq data and compared them with previously reported studies.
statements.evidence: The computational workflow is further validated by evaluating the metabolite-gene-pathway sets predicted for 18 cancer types, by using RNA-seq data publicly available, in comparison with the reported studies.
statements.note: The abstract reports this further validation across 18 cancer types with public RNA-seq data.

statements.text: Across the Pezizomycotina, atp8 and atp9 moved out of the mitochondrion into the nuclear genome.
